findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category is unset or doesn't match a category
findings.body: The query joins `site_settings` to `categories` on the `embed_category` setting value and then calls `[0]['id']` on the result. If no `embed_category` row exists (the default case, since it defaulted to ''), or its value matches no category name, the result set is empty. `[0]` then returns nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The migration aborts on most installs, and the `category_id == 0` fallback is never reached. Check `cmd_tuples` or `ntuples` before indexing.

findings.title: Migrated hosts are not normalized and the raw value is interpolated into SQL
findings.body: The old `embeddable_hosts` values are inserted verbatim, e.g. `http://eviltrout.com`, `https://example.com/1234`, or values with a trailing `\r` or whitespace. The old matcher stripped schemes and parsed URIs. The new `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` to the bare `uri.host`, so these rows never match and embedding silently breaks for existing sites after upgrade. The value is also string-interpolated into the INSERT, so any quote in it breaks the migration. Strip scheme, path and whitespace, skip blank lines, and use `quote`.

findings.title: before_validation raises on nil host
findings.body: `self.host.sub!` is called unconditionally. When the host is nil, e.g. a POST or PUT to the admin endpoint without `embeddable_host[:host]`, this raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Guard with `if host.present?` or use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)`.

findings.title: Host lookup is not truly case-insensitive and ignores ports
findings.body: The column is lowercased with `lower(host)`, but the parameter is passed as-is from `uri.host`. Ruby's URI does not downcase hosts, so a referer like `http://EvilTrout.com` won't match. The validation regex also allows a `:port` suffix, but `uri.host` excludes the port, so a host saved with a port can never match. Downcase the parameter and either reject ports or compare them.

findings.title: update/destroy with unknown id raise NoMethodError
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: ...).first` returns nil for a missing id. `host.destroy` and `save_host(nil)` then raise NoMethodError and return a 500 instead of a 404. Use `find` or `raise Discourse::NotFound`.

findings.title: Delete failures are silently swallowed
findings.body: `destroyRecord()` has no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`. If the server delete fails, the admin gets no feedback and the promise rejection is unhandled. The save action does handle errors, so delete is inconsistent with it.

findings.title: type.replace('_','-') only replaces the first underscore
findings.body: `String#replace` with a string pattern replaces only the first occurrence. Any admin model type with two or more underscores won't be normalized and will be routed to `/` instead of `/admin/`. Use `/_/g`.

findings.title: Test requests fruit 2 but the fixture always returns fruit 1
findings.body: The pretender handler for `/fruits/:id` always returns `fruits[0]`, the apple with `color_ids [1,2]`. The test asks for fruit 2, the banana with `color_ids [3]`, yet asserts two colors with ids 1 and 2. It passes only because the id is ignored, so it misrepresents what is being tested and would fail if the fixture honored the id.

findings.title: "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer tests what it says
findings.body: `expandable_first_post?` no longer depends on embeddable hosts. This test passes only because `embed_truncate` defaults to false. The test name is misleading, and the outer `before` block that `Fabricate`s a host has no effect on the behavior under test.
